subject: ap_csa
note: AP Precalculus is the day before, 2027-05-11.

exam._note: mcq_weight, frq_weight, and unit_weights describe the REAL AP exam's official section and unit weighting, for reference only. The readiness engine does not apply them: composite_pct is a flat percent-correct across all server-graded attempts with no section weighting, and readiness.per_unit_min holds every unit to the same floor regardless of its exam weight.

readiness.reuse_days_note: How long a question stays 'already answered' before it counts as evidence again, read by select.js. Sized to THIS bank, not picked round: 218 items at the ~8 answers a day of ordinary drilling is about 27 days to work through, so 28 lets the bank cycle instead of locking. It is also inside select.js's longest spaced-review interval (35 days) — a window longer than that would stop a due review being served with the very item that was missed — and below window_span_days_max / (consecutive_qualifying_mocks - 1) = 21... which it is NOT, deliberately: 218 items covers 2 disjoint 42-question sittings (84) with room to spare, so the qualifying window is satisfiable at 28. tools/build/validate.js checks that arithmetic on every build. Beyond the window select.js still serves the least-recently-seen question rather than refusing, and labels it a repeat.

_documentation_only._note: Keys below are not read anywhere in worker/src. They record intent that was never wired into the readiness engine; treat every value here as reference, not as an enforced rule.

frq_calibrated.note: Meant to say whether the FRQ grader has been validated against an officially scored College Board response. NOT read by anything: api.js passes `calibrated: false` as a literal at all three computeReadiness call sites (summarize, handleStatus, handleDashboard), so editing this key changes no output whatsoever. It sat under `readiness` with a note asserting runtime behaviour it does not have. To make it live, api.js's owner replaces those three literals with `config.readiness.frq_calibrated === true` and moves this key back up into `readiness`; readiness.js already takes `calibrated` as a parameter and needs no change. Until then the engine is hard-wired to the safe state: the frq criterion is reported as pending rather than failed, free-response evidence cannot move the number, and 100% is unreachable.

reduced_confidence_mocks_min.note: Meant to raise the required mock count when the evidence is weak (e.g. still bank-only). Not implemented — no criterion or advisory reads it.

difficulty_gap_max.note: Meant to cap how far the question bank's difficulty can drift from the official exam's. Not implemented — no criterion or advisory reads it.

historical_note: 2026 redesigned exam: 5=25%, 4=26%, 3=15%, 2=11%, 1=23%. Distribution published; raw-to-composite conversion is NOT, so C5 is unknown and these floors stay conservative.
